validity.recommendation: Re-derive this row against the real Hawiyah programme pipes; likely merge/relabel into the UBTG-1 cluster (P1910/P1911) and/or reclassify as the 1 km HUG-1 connection. Do not treat as a standalone 56 km / 56-inch dry-gas transmission line.
validity.researcher_notes: No independent source describes a 56 km, 56-inch dry-gas transmission line named or matching 'Hawiyah-UBTG-1-km0'. The gem.wiki page cites only two generic OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin PDFs (no pipeline-specific detail). The authoritative independent account of the Hawiyah pipeline programme (MEED, verified 200) describes the actual 56-inch line in this corridor as a '56-inch, 1-kilometre section between the [Hawiyah NGL] plant and the Hawiyah-Uthmaniyah gas line (HUG-1)' -- i.e. 1 km, NOT 56 km. MEED and Aramco material also describe a 56-inch RICH GAS / NGL line from the Haradh/Hawiyah increment to Uthmaniyah for deep ethane recovery, and a 24-inch / 57 km NGL line Hawiyah->Uthmaniyah -- none of which is a 56 km dry-gas trunk. The GEM '56 km' length appears conflated with the UBTG-1 km-marker scheme: the roster's P1910/P1911 ('UBTG-1-km0 -> UBTG-1-km56', both 56 km) are the km0->km56 trunk segments, and 'Hawiyah-UBTG-1-km0' reads as an artificial node-to-node label whose 56 diameter matches the HUG-1 connection and whose 56 length is borrowed from the km0->km56 span. Concern: this is plausibly a GEM-only / km-node artifact that is either a duplicate of the UBTG-1 cluster (P1910/P1911/P1898/P1899) or the mislabeled 1 km HUG-1 connection -- not an independently attestable standalone pipeline. CONFIRMED only: Saudi Aramco ownership and a gas/NGL pipeline programme out of Hawiyah toward Uthmaniyah exist. NOT confirmed: the name, the 56 km length, that it is dry transmission gas, and that it is a distinct pipe from the UBTG-1 segments.

summary: P1912 Hawiyah-UBTG-1-km0: CONCERN (existence + spec) -- no independent source supports a 56 km / 56-inch dry-gas line of this name; MEED gives the 56-inch Hawiyah->HUG-1 link as 1 km and describes the corridor's 56-inch lines as rich-gas/NGL; 56 km likely borrowed from UBTG-1 km0->km56 (P1910/P1911), so this reads as a km-node artifact / probable duplicate or mislabel.
